name: spro-core-m1

scenarios.scope: Existing T006A language row; MSEHT/MSEHL patch only. No unit creation, conversion or full CUNI maintenance.
scenarios.recovery: Reconcile first. An authorized restoration is a new apply with fresh read/text versions and the original description. Unknown receipts remain protected; no automatic retry or rollback.
scenarios.cts: Explicit open Customizing request and child task; exact T006A row key. Restoration does not remove historical CTS entries.

scenarios.scope: Dedicated customer object, unused interval, no year/subobject/buffering. Create/update bounds, not current-number assignment.
scenarios.recovery: Read-only reconciliation; no interval delete or generic rollback. Any further update requires fresh native version and approval.
scenarios.cts: Intervals are explicitly local-client-only; no transport recording or release.

scenarios.scope: EHS_CUNI_KNM/N only, fixed nine-table/nineteen-key CUNI scope: ten candidate rows and nine protected keys.
scenarios.recovery: Same persistent state directory, immutable before/effects references and original receipt hash. Configuration restore and cleanup of only owned added CTS keys are separate durable phases, run as the failure arm: recover_configuration_bc_set removes the ten rows apply_configuration_bc_set inserted, so it is never part of the happy path above. Historical activation protocol remains.
scenarios.cts: Fixed request GR2K923429/task GR2K923430; current ownership/status/source pins must still pass. No release.

supportingReads.reason: Comparison read: diffs stored classic BC Set fields against target observations. It reports drift for a BC Set instead of changing one, so no delivered write loop runs it.
Comparison read: diffs one exact internal unit key against another system. The unit-text loop patches stored text and never compares two instances.
Layout read: describes one approved customizing-tier transparent table within 64 fields. It supplies field metadata to other reads rather than advancing a loop.
Discovery read: locates IMG activities for one approved table so a caller can choose what to work on; the unit-text loop already names its own activity.
Discovery read: searches classic BC Set candidates by record metadata. The bc-knm loop works one fixed BC Set and does not search.
Discovery read: enumerates FI validation rule headers. M1 publishes no FI validation loop (see boundaries), so it stands outside every flow.
Impact read: composes a partial BC Set impact report. The bc-knm loop reads the native, guard and CTS snapshots it needs directly.
Route read: reports the fixed BF24/TBE24 product maintenance route. M1 publishes no BTE product-change loop (see boundaries).
ABI read: attests the fixed TBE24 native control blocks through the separately deployed read-only helper. It is a precondition of BTE work, not a step any published loop runs.
Route read: reports the fixed OB28 activation metadata behind an FI rule assignment. M1 publishes no FI activation loop (see boundaries).
CTS read: inspects one explicit Customizing request/task pair on request. Each published loop names its own fixed request instead.
Planning read: assembles the change and recovery review bundle for one existing customer BTE product. The activation it prepares is not delivered as a loop (see boundaries).
Planning read: prepares a controlled human workflow for CMOD, FIBF and validation/substitution work. It hands work to a person rather than closing a loop here.
Preview read: previews one exact plant configuration row after pinned type and TPMODE checks. No delivered write loop owns that table.
Preview read: previews an activation flag change for one existing customer BTE product. The BTE product-change loop is not delivered (see boundaries).
Preview read: previews the ACTIV value for one existing FI validation assignment. M1 publishes no FI activation loop (see boundaries).
Read: returns one BTE Event or Process definition with its application and customer-product handlers. BTE configuration is inspected here, never changed by a published loop.
Read: audits stored classic BC Set child references. The bc-knm loop reads its fixed nine-table CUNI scope instead.
Read: returns bounded historical references for a stored classic BC Set header. History is inspected on request, not as part of activating a BC Set.
Read: returns one IMG activity-linked standard end-user document in an explicit language. It supports a person reading about an activity; no flow depends on it.
Read: returns one exact FI validation/substitution rule by SAP ID, company code, application area and callup point. M1 publishes no FI rule change loop (see boundaries).
Discovery read: searches standard BTE dispatcher function modules by naming convention, locating handlers for inspection outside any published loop.

boundaries: API only. No GUI automation or generic standard-table writes.
Source/interface/DDIC attestations, authorization, locking, optimistic versions and durable unknown-write protection remain enforced.
Package creation and tool visibility do not authorize SAP writes, customer-object deployment, CTS cleanup, lock release, service switch or publication.
Historical private-instance acceptance does not prove acceptance of this candidate or the formal service.

FI save/recovery, BTE activation and arbitrary IMG activities are not delivered by M1. Every configuration tool the server implements is exposed; the configuration tools that contracts/verification-registry.json does not verify are declared in unverifiedTools, and every unverified tool on this surface outside that family is declared in unverifiedOutsideConfiguration. SAP acceptance of this surface is not established.

The published scenarios are the only closed loops this surface promises. Every configuration tool delivered outside them is documented in supportingReads with the role it plays, which is a statement about this contract and not a capability or acceptance claim: it does not mean the loop that tool belongs to is delivered.

Each scenario declares its two arms apart: flow is the happy path a caller runs, failurePath carries the tools that reverse the change. A reversing write is never a happy-path step, a tool belongs to exactly one arm, and a flow that writes has to run a read-only step afterwards that observes what the write changed. A closed loop that would undo itself is not a delivered business loop.

unverifiedOutsideConfiguration.reason: Reads the service's own write-recovery registry and never contacts SAP (registry method `none`). In this registry `verified` attests a SAP-side acceptance, so a tool that cannot reach SAP has no evidence path and stays `unverified` by design; the live call of 2026-10-02 returning `count 0` cannot establish the absence of SAP-side locks or of operations recorded by another service instance.
